{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=causal+tracing+strategies+for+identifying+unrecognized+reasoning+limitations+and+blind+spots+in+LLMs&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7438399\", \"title\": [\"Evaluating Theory-of-Mind Reasoning in LLMs with Temporal Causal Belief Graphs\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Higher-order theory of mind (ToM), the ability to attribute mental states to others, including their beliefs about others' beliefs, remains a persistent challenge in large language model reasoning. We introduce a benchmark of 1,000 multi-agent stories that probes higher-order theory of mind with temporal causal belief graphs. Beliefs propagate between agents node-to-node on a temporal multilayer graph. Edges can be cooperative, deceptive, trusted, or untrusted. To evaluate belief attribution, we use four metrics over the predicted graph versus the ground truth agent beliefs: final node accuracy, time-respecting node accuracy, temporal edge F1, and normalized structural distance. We also measure common knowledge errors and a reality bias, where LLMs default to the true world state even when an agent's belief diverges from it. This paper contributes a benchmark and an evaluation framework for higher-order theory-of-mind reasoning.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7438399\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1108/sd-10-2016-0142\", \"title\": [\"Missing links in effective emerging markets strategies\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:sec>\\n<jats:title content-type=\\\"abstract-subheading\\\">Purpose</jats:title>\\n<jats:p>This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies.</jats:p>\\n</jats:sec>\\n<jats:sec>\\n<jats:title content-type=\\\"abstract-subheading\\\">Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>\\n<jats:p>This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context.</jats:p>\\n</jats:sec>\\n<jats:sec>\\n<jats:title content-type=\\\"abstract-subheading\\\">Findings</jats:title>\\n<jats:p>Clayton Christenson in <jats:italic>The Innovator’s Dilemma</jats:italic> (1997) teaches us that many firms think they are too big to fail, or cannot fail, despite the fact they can see the competition coming from miles away. Whether it is hiding in plain sight, or they cannot see the wood for the trees, there seems to be a feeling in large corporations that while some organizations may be able to gain some competitive advantage, they will never be able to scale this up. This has been, of course, a huge error – just ask Kodak and hundreds of other firms who failed to heed the warning signs.</jats:p>\\n</jats:sec>\\n<jats:sec>\\n<jats:title content-type=\\\"abstract-subheading\\\">Practical/implications</jats:title>\\n<jats:p>The paper provides strategic insights and practical thinking that have influenced some of the world’s leading organizations.</jats:p>\\n</jats:sec>\\n<jats:sec>\\n<jats:title content-type=\\\"abstract-subheading\\\">Originality/value</jats:title>\\n<jats:p>The briefing saves busy executives and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.</jats:p>\\n</jats:sec>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1108/sd-10-2016-0142\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2017, 1, 9]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1079/9781800620575.0009\", \"title\": [\"Identifying the causal agent of leaf spots and blights\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1079/9781800620575.0009\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2023, 7, 30]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.5145114\", \"title\": [\"Blind Spots in Broad Strokes: Caveats for the Use of LLMs in Marketing Research\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5145114\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "c9f7134e877038a1a1ae30bf05d8d6e1d16df5adb48b62adfa905ea15a1badcd", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unrecognized_reasoning_limits", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.7438399", "doi:10.1108/sd-10-2016-0142", "doi:10.1079/9781800620575.0009", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.5145114"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7438399", "https://doi.org/10.1108/sd-10-2016-0142", "https://doi.org/10.1079/9781800620575.0009", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5145114"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
